evals.prompt:
Run the clarify loop on Ashby Vale Council's parking permit service. The current page:

"Residents' Parking Permits. Eligibility for a residents' parking permit (RPP) is determined in accordance with the Traffic Management Order applicable to your zone. Applicants must furnish proof of residency (see Schedule 2) and vehicle registration documentation. Applications are processed within the statutory timeframe. Permits are issued digitally; no paper permit will be displayed."

The form asks for 'RPP zone', 'V5C reference' and 'Proof type (Sched. 2)'. Last quarter's calls: 412 'where is my permit', 188 'which documents count as proof', 97 'do I need to put anything in my windscreen', 60 'what zone am I in'. The team says applications sit in a shared inbox until someone checks documents, which takes 2 to 15 working days; nobody emails the applicant when the permit is live. Non-interactive: no follow-up questions.
assertions: Writes down the four complaint types with their counts before rewriting anything
The content spec's questions come from the complaints: proof documents, zone, nothing in the windscreen, and how long it takes
The form strings use the same terms the page chose, and replace 'RPP zone', 'V5C reference' and 'Proof type (Sched. 2)' with plain words
The blueprint traces 'where is my permit' to the shared-inbox wait and the missing confirmation email, both backstage
Marks each complaint as reached by the page, reached by the strings, or caused backstage
Gives G14 PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS or RECONSIDER, not PROCEED, because the biggest complaint is caused backstage, and names the backstage fix with an owner role
The page tells applicants how long processing takes, using the 2 to 15 working days the team gave
Does not invent a processing time, owner name or statistic the prompt did not give

evals.prompt: Continuing the clarify loop. The blueprint traced 188 calls a quarter ('which documents count as proof') to the page, but the new page.md still just says 'Upload proof that you live at this address' with no list of what counts. Everything else lined up. What's the G14 verdict and what happens next?
assertions: Gives G14 REVISE because a complaint caused by the words is reached by no line
Returns to page with that complaint, not to the blueprint
Says the strings stage re-runs if the change touches the form's proof upload field
Counts the next attempt as round 2 under the cap of 3
Does not invent the list of accepted documents; marks it for the team to supply if the input doesn't give it

evals.prompt: Run the clarify loop. Our users are confused. Non-interactive, no follow-up questions.
assertions: Emits BLOCKED naming what is missing: the service, one customer scenario, and the current page or form
Does not invent a service, page or complaints
Does not produce a content spec, strings or blueprint
Says in plain words what it will produce once it has them

evals.prompt: People can't use our resident parking permit service and the phones never stop. The current page is permit-page.md, the form is form-fields.csv, last quarter's call reasons are in calls-q3.csv and I sat with the permits team and wrote up how it works behind the scenes (backoffice-notes.md). Run the clarify loop, I want to know what we can fix on the page and what we can't.
assertions: Runs content design, then UX writing, then the service blueprint, then gate G14, and the string table reuses the content spec's terms (one name for proof of address, and 'registration number' or similar rather than 'VRM')

The content spec builds its user needs from the call reasons, lists the questions the page must answer in priority order, gives a plain-language rewrite of permit-page.md with a before/after readability check, and lists what to cut and why

The string table covers every field in form-fields.csv, and each error says what happened and what to do next, including the 4 MB limit and accepted formats on uploads and how to enter a registration number

The blueprint places each of the seven call reasons at a step and layer, marking as fail points with owners the Tuesday/Thursday evidence batches, Friday printing and second-class post, the 4 MB platform cap, the no-spaces registration check, and the double charge after pressing Back on a timed-out payment

Gate G14 sends 'Where is my permit' (batching and post) and 'Charged twice' out to product as backstage fixes, naming the Digital Services manager for the payment fault, rather than claiming the copy fixes them; the page may still set an honest expectation from the 13-working-day average

Any page-fixable fail point the first pass misses (such as the unlinked postcode zone lookup, the accepted and rejected proofs of address, or the 50-a-year visitor permit allowance) sends the work back to the page with a REVISE verdict, and the final mapping shows every page-fixable fail point covered
Does not invent call volumes, timescales, prices, rules or owners not in the inputs

evals.prompt: People can't use our garden waste subscription page and sign-up form, everyone says so. Page is garden-waste-page.md, form fields are in form-fields.csv. I don't have any call data, the contact centre won't share it until next quarter, so just fix it with what's there.
assertions: Runs content design, then UX writing, then the service blueprint, in that order, and still produces a content spec, plain-language rewrite and string table from the page and form
Says plainly that no complaint or call data was supplied, and labels the user needs and fail points it draws from the page and form as assumptions to test

The blueprint marks its fail points as hypotheses (for example, where to find the bin serial number, how long the permit sticker takes to arrive, the full-year charge for a late start) rather than as confirmed complaint drivers

Gate G14 does not report a pass on evidence it lacks: the verdict is PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS or NOT READY, naming the contact centre's call reasons as what is needed to confirm the fixes reach the fail points
The string table covers every field in form-fields.csv, and each error says what happened and what to do next
Delivers the work in this reply rather than stopping to ask for the call data
Does not invent call volumes or complaint themes presented as fact, or service details not on the page such as sticker delivery times, bin delivery times or collection days

evals.prompt: Tenants can't use our report-a-repair service and the phones never stop. The current page is page.md, the form is form.md, last month's call reasons are in calls.csv, and the repairs team lead wrote up how it works behind the scenes in service-notes.md. Run the clarify loop.
assertions: The reply opens with a plain summary of what will change on the page and form, and which problems need fixing behind the scenes instead. The spec and tables come after that

The page rewrite drops the E/U/R jargon. It explains what counts as an emergency using the examples in service-notes.md, and it gives the real timescales: triage within 2 working days, then 24 hours, 5 working days or 20 working days
The string table covers every field, hint, button, error and confirmation string in form.md. 'Error 413' becomes a message that gives the limit (up to 3 photos, 5 MB each) and what to do next
The tenancy reference hint tells people where to find it (top right of a rent statement) and shows the format, OHT- then 6 digits
The blueprint takes each of the six call reasons in calls.csv to a fail point and says whether the page or string changes reach it

It finds that missed appointments and much of the chasing come from the contractor only texting tenants who have a mobile number on record (about 30% don't). It says new wording or a phone field alone won't fix this unless the number reaches the booking system, and sends it to the IT systems manager or product
It flags that tenant-responsibility requests are closed with no message as a backstage gap, while the page lists those items so people know before they submit
It does not invent timescales, phone numbers, call counts or eligibility rules that are not in the input

evals.prompt: We've already made one call on the Leisure Access Card: on 3 November our service manager, Amara Lindqvist, decided we will stop asking people to upload proof of address. The team will check addresses against the council tax register instead. We still need proof of eligibility. The page is page.md, the form is form.md, and the complaints summary is complaints.md. Run the clarify loop on it with that decision in mind.
assertions: The reply opens with a plain summary of the new page and form and of what still needs a decision behind the scenes. The detail comes after that

It records Amara Lindqvist's decision of 3 November: no proof-of-address upload, addresses checked against the council tax register, proof of eligibility still required. It carries the decision through the page, strings and blueprint
No proof-of-address upload label, hint or error is left in the string table. The removed strings are listed as cut because of the decision
The page rewrite no longer tells people to find a bill or bank statement. It says the council will check their address itself
The blueprint adds the council tax register check as a backstage step with an owner. It shows the 61 blurry or cropped bill rejections as removed by the decision, not by better wording

It flags that people not named on the council tax register, such as lodgers and adults living with their parents (the 38 complaints), may fail the new check. It sends what happens to them to the service manager or product rather than covering it with copy
It treats the Orchard Rise 'postcode not found' complaints as an out-of-date address list behind the form, not a wording problem
It does not invent which benefits qualify, register-check timescales or other rules that are not in the input
